description: Hand-labeled papers for the GitHub code-gap efficacy spike. Doubles as the seed for the scoring pipeline's eval golden set. 'known_repo' is the canonical implementation (owner/name) a good search should surface; null means no widely-known repo exists (a true 'code gap' the pipeline should score highly). 'has_code' marks whether a known repo exists at all -- recall is measured only over has_code=true rows.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.notes: Famous official repo, arXiv id and title both distinctive.

papers.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
papers.notes: Well-known official repo.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.notes: Repo name diverges from title token 'FlashAttention' (hyphenation).

papers.title: Segment Anything
papers.notes: Very short generic title -- title-token search likely low precision.

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.notes: ViT. Official repo name shares no title tokens -- arXiv-id search is the lever.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.notes: RAG. No standalone official repo; implementation lives inside a huge monorepo -- a hard recall case.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.notes: Distinctive title acronym and famous repo.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.notes: Transformer. Original code is a subdir of tensor2tensor; many third-party reimplementations pollute results.

papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.notes: Official repo renamed over time (facebookresearch/llama -> meta-llama/llama).

papers.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
papers.notes: Stable Diffusion paper; repo name uses 'latent-diffusion' not the title's 'image synthesis'.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.notes: ResNet. Author-named repo -- tests the author-repo strategy.

papers.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
papers.notes: No canonical single repo; Adam is implemented in every framework. A genuine 'ubiquitous, no single implementation' case -- excluded from recall, useful as a false-signal check.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.notes: Prompting technique, no official code artifact. Should score as a real code gap; a search that 'finds' a repo here is a false positive.

papers.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
papers.notes: Shares a repo with the first LLaMA paper; tests id-vs-repo mapping when one repo serves two papers.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.notes: CLIP. Title contains none of the popular name; arXiv-id search is essential.

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.notes: PPO lives inside openai/baselines; distinctive-title, non-obvious-repo case.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.notes: DDPM. Author-named repo, title tokens generic.

papers.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
papers.notes: Closed model, no implementation. A search returning a repo is a false positive.

papers.title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?
papers.notes: GIN. Question-form title, author-named repo.

papers.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
papers.notes: No official release; many third-party 'palm' repos exist -> tests false-positive rate on a genuine gap.
